records.title: Chile President Lays Out Security Agenda and Vandal Black List
records.summary: Chile President José Antonio Kast said in his first State of the Nation address that he’ll roll out new public security measures in coming weeks, including one to create a black list of “vandals” who would lose the right to some social benefits.

records.title: South Africa Gasoline Prices Hit Record With Relief Rollback
records.summary: South African gasoline prices are set to reach a record high this month after the government rolled back some temporary relief measures that had cushioned consumers against fuel-cost increases sparked by the Iran war.

records.title: India May Scale Back UK FTA Concessions Over Steel Duties
records.summary: India may reconsider some concessions under the free trade agreement it struck with the UK if its steel exports do not receive relief from proposed safeguard duties, a senior government official in New Delhi said.

records.title: US Manufacturing Activity Expands by Most in Four Years
records.summary: US manufacturing activity expanded in May at the fastest pace in four years, bolstered by a pickup in new orders and production.

records.title: Peru Inflation Unexpectedly Slows, Still Running Over Target
records.summary: Inflation in Peru’s capital came in below expectations in May, but remained above the central bank’s target range for the third straight month.

records.title: South Africa Factory Sentiment Worsens as Demand Fades
records.summary: South Africa’s manufacturer sentiment worsened in May as demand slumped and supply disruptions due to the Iran war continued.

records.title: Apollo’s Slok Says AI Will Dash Warsh’s Hopes for Quick Rate Cut
records.summary: The build-out for artificial intelligence will be inflationary in the early going, preventing new Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh from cutting interest rates as quickly as he has suggested should be possible, according to Torsten Slok of Apollo Global Management Inc.

records.title: Chile Economy Starts Second Quarter With Minimal Monthly Growth
records.summary: Chile’s economic activity barely rose at the start of the second quarter, the central bank reported on Monday, marking the latest in a series of disappointing indicators in one of Latin America’s richest nations.

records.title: India’s Factory Output Expands 4.9% Under Revised Data Series
records.summary: India’s factory output grew 4.9% in April from a year earlier under a revised data series designed to better reflect structural changes in Asia’s third-largest economy.

records.title: How the AI Boom Is Rewiring Asia’s Growth Model
records.summary: The artificial-intelligence capex boom is fueling gains for South Korea and Taiwan and rewiring the region’s growth model.

records.title: Trump’s Trade Chief Takes a Globalist Victory Lap
records.summary: Jamieson Greer takes his defense of Trump’s tariffs to the heart of globalization’s intellectual base

records.title: Bond Trader Bets on Fed Hike Poised for Gut Check From Jobs Data
records.summary: Bond traders are looking to a key jobs report this week to confirm their wagers that the US economy is strong enough to push the Federal Reserve to lift interest rates by next year.

records.title: India Holds Jet Fuel Prices Steady After Airline Plea
records.summary: India’s state-owned oil refiners have kept jet fuel prices steady for local flights following a plea from airlines to hold off on further hikes as they grapple with the fallout from the Iran war.

records.title: China Leads Economic Shift to Industrial ‘Doping,’ OECD Says
records.summary: Industrial subsidies are reshaping the global economy with China standing out as a provider of state support that risks harmful distortions, according to new data from the OECD.

records.title: ECB Says Consumer Price Expectations Ease But Stay Elevated
records.summary: Euro-area consumers’ expectations for inflation in three years fell slightly in April, offering some relief to the European Central Bank, though policymakers are still likely to raise interest rates next week.

records.title: UK Factory Growth Spurt Set to Be Short-Lived, PMI Shows
records.summary: UK factories grew at the fastest pace in four years as the industry sought to get ahead of price increases and supply strains triggered by the Middle East conflict, a key survey found.

records.title: Revolving-Door Politics Erode Peru’s Mining Appeal Ahead of Vote
records.summary: Rich deposits and low costs have made Peru a mining superpower. But as Peruvians prepare to choose their ninth president in a decade, the industry is losing competitiveness just as demand for critical minerals accelerates.

records.title: A 20% Housing Drop Still Leaves Canadians Locked Out of Market
records.summary: Canada’s housing market has plunged into one of its sharpest-ever corrections. Canadians say it hasn’t gone far enough.

records.title: EU Proposes Tax Simplification Measures in Bid to Boost Business
records.summary: The European Union will propose a streamlining of rules and exemptions in the area of taxation, its latest effort to reduce bureaucracy.

records.title: Odd Lots: The Hidden Plumbing of Commodity Finance (Podcast)
records.summary: We talk about the commodity supply chain all the time. We talk about the ports and the trucks and the ships and all of that. records.title: Germany’s Manufacturers Eked Out Slight Expansion in May
records.summary: Activity in Germany’s key manufacturing sector rose slightly in May, contrasting with an initial reading that showed a small decline.

records.title: Swiss Economy Grew Less Than Estimated at Start of the Year
records.summary: Switzerland’s economy grew slightly less than initially reported in the first quarter, weighed down by stalling consumer demand and a drop in investment.

records.title: Morocco Pips South Africa as Continent’s Top Industrial Economy
records.summary: Morocco overtook South Africa as the continent’s most industrialized economy last year as it upgrades its offering, diversifies exports and implements growth policies, a report showed.

records.title: Bank of France to Cut 2026 Growth Forecast, Villeroy Says
records.summary: The Bank of France will lower its growth forecasts later this month after a disappointing start to the year and as tensions in the Middle East drag on, outgoing Governor Francois Villeroy de Galhau said.

records.title: Japan Adds to Steel Scrutiny With Probes on China, Taiwan, Korea
records.summary: Japan has launched an anti-dumping probe into imports of key steel products shipped from China, South Korea and Taiwan, adding to signs of trade stress in a sector suffering from global overcapacity.

records.title: China’s Private Factory Gauge Slows as Economy Softens
records.summary: China’s manufacturing activity slowed in May, according to a private survey of export-oriented firms, in line with an official gauge that suggests the world’s second-largest economy is losing some steam.

records.title: ECB’s Schnabel Sees Risk of Unanchored Inflation Views From War
records.summary: The European Central Bank can no longer look through the inflationary impact of the war in Iran as price pressures spread beyond energy and the risk of unanchored inflation expectations rises, according to Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel.

records.title: South Korea’s Export Momentum Continues, Backing BOK’s Hawkish Case
records.summary: South Korea’s exports extended their strong run in May, reinforcing the central bank’s increasingly hawkish stance as booming semiconductor demand continues to underpin growth despite rising geopolitical and inflation risks.

records.title: Japan’s Firms Cut Spending Over Iran Stress Even as Profits Firm
records.summary: Japan’s biggest companies reduced capital spending in the first quarter even as ordinary profits at manufacturers reached a record, as emerging uncertainty from escalating turbulence in the Middle East clouded prospects for future growth.

records.title: Powell Says Fed Credibility Lost If President Can Fire Officials
records.summary: Former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell said the US central bank would lose the credibility that’s required to support a strong and stable economy if any president were free to dismiss Fed officials over policy disagreements.
